title: The modification of cardiometabolic and pro-atherogenic parameters through weight-reducing interventions and their influence on endothelial foam cell formation, vascular calcification potential, and cardiomyocyte function as a model of the controlled normalization of the metabolic state.
summary: This study investigates how different weight-loss treatments in people with severe obesity affect heart and blood vessel health, metabolism, and inflammation in the body. The treatments include bariatric surgery, weight-loss medication (GLP-1 receptor agonists), and conservative therapy consisting of dietary changes, physical activity, and behavioral support. Participants receive their treatment as part of routine medical care, independent of the study. For research purposes, additional blood and urine samples are collected, questionnaires on quality of life and social situation are completed, and non-invasive examinations of heart and vascular function are performed. These assessments take place at the beginning of the study and after 3, 6, and 12 months. A final follow-up telephone interview is conducted after five years. The aim of the study is to better understand how weight loss can help prevent cardiovascular disease and which biological mechanisms are involved. In the long term, the results are intended to contribute to improved treatment for people with obesity.

interventions.name: Arm 1: BMI ≥40 kg/m² and bariatric procedure independent of the study in accordance with the German S3 guideline Surgery of Obesity and Metabolic Diseases.
Arm 2: BMI ≥35 and <40 kg/m² who are treated with a GLP-1 receptor agonist independent of the study
Arm 3: BMI ≥35 kg/m² and conservative therapy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Arm 1: BMI ≥ 40 kg/m² undergoing bariatric surgery according to S3 guidelines.
Arm 2: BMI ≥ 35 and < 40 kg/m² treated with GLP-1 receptor agonists.
Arm 3: BMI ≥ 35 kg/m² receiving conservative multimodal therapy
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under 18 years of age, coronary artery disease, active or previous malignancy, manifest diabetes mellitus, end-stage renal insufficiency (GFR < 15 mL/min), rheumatologic diseases, known psoriasis, and pregnancy
